transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess they brought me in because at the warehouse I keep doing things that don’t make sense to people. I’ll freeze with my arms up near the forklift, copy the beeping and the hand signals, or move boxes in these little patterns. Even when everybody’s yelling at me to stop, I just keep doing it.
When did these behaviors, like freezing and copying movements, first start happening?
About six months, I think. That’s when the talking got confusing too, and the stuff at the warehouse started getting strange.
During these past six months, have you experienced persistent feelings of sadness or depression?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed feeling sad all the time or anything like that.
Have there been times over these past six months when you felt unusually energetic, had racing thoughts, or felt you didn't need to sleep?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed being unusually energetic or going without sleep.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions or physical illnesses?
No, not that I know of. I haven’t been diagnosed with any physical illnesses.
Have you used any alcohol, recreational drugs, or new medications since these symptoms began?
I’m not sure what would count as new medication. I haven’t really noticed anything like that.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with prominent catatonic symptoms including posturing (freezing with arms raised), echopraxia/echolalia (mimicking sounds and hand signals), mannerisms/stereotypies (arranging boxes in fixed patterns), and negativism (resisting verbal commands to stop), alongside disorganized speech.
